title: Degradation-Aware AC-Constrained Day-Ahead Active and Reactive Power Scheduling of Battery Energy Storage Systems in Active Distribution Networks
abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources requires battery energy storage systems (BESSs) to be scheduled economically while preserving network security and accounting for battery-life consumption. This work’s primary technical contribution is an integrated, degradation-aware framework for coordinated day-ahead active–reactive power dispatch of multiple BESS units in active distribution networks. The formulation minimizes grid-energy purchases, PV and BESS operation and maintenance costs, and monetized cycling and calendar degradation while enforcing nonlinear AC power-flow equations, voltage and branch-current limits, converter apparent-power capability, non-ideal state-of-charge dynamics, and terminal-energy requirements. Each candidate 24-h SoC trajectory is processed through a Rainflow-based semi-empirical aging model, allowing degradation to be included directly in the fitness evaluation. SELGO is employed as the optimization engine and coupled with a parallel successive-approximation AC power-flow evaluator. The framework is assessed through 100 independent executions under deterministic operating conditions and 100 stochastic demand and PV-generation scenarios in a modified 33-bus system, together with 100 stochastic scenarios in a modified 69-bus system. SELGO is compared with AJAYA, GA, MVO, PSO, and TDE under equivalent models, constraints, scenarios, and parameter-tuning conditions. Among the evaluated methods, SELGO yields the smallest mean operating cost for each of the three analyzed cases, reducing the corresponding base costs by 2.2015%, 2.4017%, and 3.0108%, respectively, while satisfying voltage, thermal, converter, and inter-temporal BESS constraints. The cumulative ablation analysis also supports the conditional benefit of the complete SELGO architecture. Across the analyzed cases, cycling intensity ranges from 0.7690 to 0.8386 EFC/day and daily aging from 6.4864×10−5 to 7.5160×10−5 day−1. Under the repeated-day assumption, the 80% SoH threshold is reached after 5.9756–6.9238 years, whereas the corresponding interval for 70% SoH is 10.8433–12.5639 years; these values are intended for comparative aging interpretation rather than as field-life predictions. The results show that the framework identifies low-cost, AC-feasible schedules while explicitly quantifying the associated battery-life consumption.
title_zh: Degradation-Aware AC-Constrained Day-Ahead Active and Reactive Power Scheduling of Battery Energy Storage Systems in Active Distribution Networks

title: Coordinated Sizing of Transformer and Hybrid Energy Storage Systems for PV-Integrated Ultra-Fast EV Charging Stations Considering Battery Degradation
abstract: Ultra-fast charging stations can impose substantial short-term power fluctuations and high transformer capacity requirements on distribution networks. To address the coupled planning and operational challenges of such stations, this study proposes a planning-operation coordinated sizing framework for a photovoltaic-integrated ultra-fast charging station. Unlike many existing approaches that address transformer sizing, energy storage configuration, and battery degradation separately or only partially couple them, the proposed framework jointly determines transformer capacity, battery capacity, and supercapacitor capacity while incorporating battery cycling degradation into the long-term storage cost evaluation. Representative charging scenarios are extracted from historical charging-load data and used for capacity planning. At the planning level, the average daily comprehensive cost is minimized by coordinating transformer investment, hybrid energy storage investment, operating cost, and degradation-dependent battery lifetime. At the operation level, battery and supercapacitor dispatch is optimized considering both operating economy and grid-connected power fluctuation. The upper-level sizing problem is solved using quantum-behaved particle swarm optimization. Sobol-sequence initialization and a nonlinear contraction-expansion coefficient are adopted in the implementation to enhance the distribution of the initial population and adjust the search range during the iterative process. The lower-level mixed-integer linear programming problem is solved using Gurobi. In the studied commercial-area case, the proposed hybrid energy storage configuration reduces the transformer capacity from 326 kVA to 201 kVA. Compared with the no-storage scheme, total costs are reduced by 14.9% and 14.3%, while the absolute deviations of grid-connected power are reduced by 93.4% and 94.8% for the two representative days. Compared with battery-only storage, daily battery cycle counts are further reduced by 60.5% and 65.2%. The results demonstrate that the proposed coordinated sizing framework can simultaneously reduce infrastructure capacity requirements and operating costs, improve grid integration performance, and alleviate battery cycling degradation in PV-integrated ultra-fast charging stations.
title_zh: Coordinated Sizing of Transformer and Hybrid Energy Storage Systems for PV-Integrated Ultra-Fast EV Charging Stations Considering Battery Degradation

title: A novel method for mechanical battery abuse testing: Planetary mill calorimetric evaluation of all-solid-state battery materials and their safety
abstract: This work presents a novel quantitative calorimeter-mill methodology for ASSB materials that quantitatively measures energy release by combining ball milling with calorimetry and pressure monitoring during extreme mechanical activation. The method accounts for the mechanical milling contribution using an operational reference. Applied to a shredded cathode consisting of delithiated state of charge 100% (SOC 100) Li x Ni 0.83 Mn z Co 0.17-z O 2 (x < 1, z < 0.17) (NMC), Al current collector, binder and conductive carbon together with systematically chosen amounts of Li 6 PS 5 Cl representing different catholyte compositions, the method quantifies composition-dependent energy release and gas evolution under extreme mechanical abuse. The method revealed that a shredded, delithiated NMC cathode showed substantial reactivity (2799 ± 159 J/g (NMC) ) with significant gas evolution, while Li 6 PS 5 Cl electrolyte addition enhanced the energy release and reduced the required mechanical activation and the gas generation. The calorimeter-mill approach provides a quantitative framework for establishing worst-case energy boundaries and enabling early-stage safety decisions in battery material development.
title_zh: A novel method for mechanical battery abuse testing: Planetary mill calorimetric evaluation of all-solid-state battery materials and their safety
